title: Testing neuromuscular feedback therapy in patients with chronic spinal cord injury and residual motor function in the lower extremities compared to "conventional" therapy
summary:
This study investigates a new therapy option for patients with persistent paraplegia and preserved residual function in the lower extremities. The aim is to prove that neuromuscular feedback therapy using a special exoskeleton (HAL® (Hybrid Assistive Limb) exoskeleton) improves walking ability even after more than a year of paralysis. Acute spinal cord injury is usually followed by treatment and rehabilitation in specialised spinal cord injury centres. This also includes special gait training on a treadmill. This training can improve walking ability, but the benefits in everyday life are often limited. There are also other therapies based on neurophysiological methods such as Vojta, Bobath and other physiotherapeutic measures. 

Neuromuscular feedback therapy records minimal electrical signals from the muscles and actively supports movement. This allows patients to control the walking process themselves, which enables more effective therapy. The HAL® exoskeleton is a CE-certified medical device that is suitable for the treatment of people with minimal residual function in the legs, regardless of the severity of the paralysis. Previous studies have shown that neuromuscular feedback therapy can bring about functional improvements in neurological deficits. The study compares the effect of neuromuscular feedback therapy using the HAL® exoskeleton with the effect of conventional forms of therapy at a comparable intensity of application.
conditions: Paraparesis and paraplegia, unspecified: chronic incomplete paraplegia

interventions.name: Intervention: neuromuscular feedback therapy with the HAL® exoskeleton over 12 weeks with 5 appointments per week of 60 minutes each.

Control intervention: therapies for spinal cord syndrome that can be prescribed in accordance with the Remedies Directive: physiotherapy (KG), KG in the exercise pool, KG CNS (Vojta, Bobath, PNF) and relevant occupational therapies over 12 weeks with 5 appointments per week of 60 min each

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. chronic, incomplete cervical, thoracic or lumbar paraplegia or complete paraplegia with preserved residual voluntary motor function in the lower extremities
2. more than 1 year after the onset of paraplegia
3. treatment at the expense of the GKV
4. height ≥ 150 and ≤ 190 cm, body weight ≥ 40 and ≤ 100 kg
5. age ≥ 18 and ≤ 75 years
6. no further improvement in walking ability to be expected with conventional therapy in line with the guidelines
Exclusion criteria:
1. contractures
2. massive spinal spasms
3. cardiac devices or other electronic implants that are impaired by the use of the exoskeleton
4. pre-existing conditions that lead to an increased risk for patients, such as
5. high-grade osteoporosis or condition after spontaneous fractures, not fully consolidated fractures
6. coronary heart disease, pulmonary embolism in the past
7. neurological diseases such as Parkinson's disease, epilepsy, severe dementia
8. acute psychiatric illnesses (e.g. depression, bipolar disorder, anxiety disorder, etc.), alcohol or drug addiction
9. decubital ulceration
10. more than 5 training sessions with the HAL exoskeleton in the past
11. pregnancy and breastfeeding
12. lack of language comprehension or lack of capacity to give consent
